name: Glaucous-Firth
description: Cloud-architecture stacks to the horizon in every direction, ammonia cirrus above, sulfurous murk below. Great storm eyes stare up out of the depths, unhurried and permanent.
Downward the pressure builds into black liquid air; upward, the storms scream past at jet speeds. There is no calm layer to stand in, only depths that tolerate visitors briefly.
Geologists argue about the strata here: several layers appear deposited out of order, as if the planet's history were shuffled like cards.
Survey contracts pay double for reasons nobody writes down. Veterans read the fine print, then read the survivors.
